title: C_d(Φ,V)[φ_x] is supported in B(Σ)_x
body_html:
Support of $\phi_x$-isotypic chains

Lemma. Assume (T3) and (T4). For $x \in A$, every element of $C_d(\Phi, V)[\phi_x]$ has support contained in $\BSigma_x := K_x \cdot A$. In particular, $C_d(\Phi, V)[\phi_x]$ is a submodule of $C_d(\BSigma_x) \otimes V$.

Hypothesis tightness. Only (T3) ($G$-equivariance) and (T4) (intertwiner) are used. (T1), (T2), (T5) and any of (K·) play no role in this lemma.
proof_html:
Recall the explicit chain-complex form (Chain complex C_•(Φ, V) of φ-isotypic chains): $$C_d(\Phi, V) \;=\; \bigoplus_{\mathcal F \in [\![\BSigma]\!]_d} \mathcal F \otimes V[\phi_{\mathcal F}].$$ Projecting to the $\phi_x$-isotypic component for the action of $K_{x,+}$ at the stalk gives $$C_d(\Phi, V)[\phi_x] \;=\; \bigoplus_{\mathcal F \in [\![\BSigma]\!]_d} \mathcal F \otimes \bigl(V[\phi_{\mathcal F}] \cap V[\phi_x]\bigr).$$ So a $d$-cell $\mathcal F$ contributes a non-zero term to $C_d(\Phi, V)[\phi_x]$ only when $V[\phi_{\mathcal F}] \cap V[\phi_x] \ne 0$, i.e.\ when there is a non-zero vector simultaneously $\phi_{\mathcal F}$-isotypic for $K_{\mathcal F, +}$ and $\phi_x$-isotypic for $K_{x,+}$. The vector lies in $V[\phi_x|{K{\mathcal F, +} \cap K_{x,+}}] = V[\phi_{\mathcal F}|{K{\mathcal F, +} \cap K_{x,+}}]$, so $$\Hom_{K_{\mathcal F, +} \cap K_{x,+}}\bigl(\phi_{\mathcal F},\, \phi_x\bigr) \ne 0. \tag{$\ast$}$$

Apply (T4). Write $\mathcal F = g\mathcal F_0$ for some $\mathcal F_0 \in [\![A]\!]_d$ and $g \in G$. Then $K_{\mathcal F, +} = {}^g K_{\mathcal F_0, +}$ and $\phi_{\mathcal F} = {}^g \phi_{\mathcal F_0}$ by (T3), so $(\ast)$ becomes $\Hom_{{}^g K_{\mathcal F_0, +} \cap K_{x,+}}({}^g \phi_{\mathcal F_0},\, \phi_x) \ne 0$. By the intertwiner axiom (T4) ([[node:coefficient_systems.semisimple_character_T_axioms]]), $$g \in K_x \cdot M \cdot K_{\mathcal F_0} \;\Longrightarrow\; g \mathcal F_0 \in K_x \cdot \mathcal B(M).$$

Conclude. By The K_x-orbit subset B(Σ)_x := K_x · A, $\BSigma_x = K_x \cdot A = K_x \cdot \mathcal B(M)$ as subsets of $\BSigma$ (the apartment $A$ equals $\mathcal B(M)$ embedded via the canonical $M = G^{(0)}$-action). Hence $\mathcal F = g\mathcal F_0 \in K_x \cdot \mathcal B(M) = \BSigma_x$, and every non-trivial summand of $C_d(\Phi, V)[\phi_x]$ has its underlying cell in $\BSigma_x$. $\square$

Remark (where (T4) really matters). It is exactly (T4) — the intertwiner hypothesis on $\Phi$ — that forces the support to lie in the $K_x$-translate of the apartment. Without (T4), the $\phi_x$-isotypic subspace could pick up contributions from $G$-translates of $A$ unrelated to $K_x$, and the geometric structure of the §7.2 argument (in particular the apartment-reduction of cartesian unit-iso) would collapse. After Fintzen 2021, the corrected formulation of (T4) for tame data is in [Dat–Fintzen 2026 §2]; the proof here works verbatim under that corrected form.

This support lemma is the geometric prerequisite for the contraction extension acting on $C_d(\Phi, V)[\phi_x]$ — see Contraction c on C_d(Φ, V)[φ_x].
